messages:
maya: heads up — customer hit a hard break when they ran the Cloudflare Worker quickstart after yesterday's publish.
alex: what error are they seeing?
maya: `TypeError: (0 , _inference.default) is not a function` at startup when doing `import inference from '@redwood/inference'`.
sam: that screams ESM default export missing. Cloudflare is strict ESM-only.
tia: we recently changed the conditional exports map; maybe the esm entry now only has named exports. We used to have a default-y shim.
ben: runtime interop is messy: bundlers + Node + edge runtimes disagree on default vs named. If our ESM build doesn't `export default`, `import foo from` will be undefined in strict ESM envs.
alex: quick summary of our builds: we emit dist/esm (module) and dist/cjs (commonjs). package.json exports currently map import->esm, require->cjs. but looks like the published package didn't include the ESM default shape.
maya: customer used the starter unchanged so this is a regression for them.
sam: mitigation idea: ship a small edge adapter file and ensure the ESM build includes `export default createClient` explicitly. Also add a worker condition to exports so CF picks a compatible file.
tia: proposed exports snippet: "exports": { ".": { "worker": "./dist/edge/index.mjs", "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" }, "./package.json": { "default": "./package.json" } }
ben: and add `types` pointers: top-level `types` -> `./dist/esm/index.d.ts` and also `exports.".".types` to be robust for TS consumers.
alex: implementation notes:
- make sure dist/edge/index.mjs re-exports default: `import client from '../esm/index.mjs'; export default client; export * from '../esm/index.mjs';`
- ensure the esm build source explicitly has `export default createClient` (not just `export { createClient }`).
- CJS build should be a real transpiled CJS bundle (not a runtime shim that tries to require .mjs).
sam: CI additions: smoke tests that pack the npm tarball and run small sanity imports:
  1) Node ESM import default + named (node --input-type=module runner)
  2) Node CJS `require()` test on supported Node versions
  3) Minimal Cloudflare worker compatibility test: esbuild bundle + run in `miniflare` or `wrangler` headless runner
  4) Deno import test via `deno run --reload` on a tiny sample
tia: we should gate publishing on those checks. release-bot: do it.
release-bot: automated: publishing pipeline now requires `smoke/cf-compat` and `smoke/deno-compat` checks to pass before npm publish.
maya: short-term customer unblock: hotfix publish that restores default export in esm and adds edge adapter.
ben: docs: update quickstart to recommend named import `import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference'` to be safer while we roll out the fix, and update sample apps.
alex: I'll open a PR with the ESM default export + edge adapter today and add the package.json exports update. ETA a few hours.
sam: I'll add the smoke CI job (miniflare + deno + node matrix). ETA tomorrow am.
tia: also add a test that verifies `types` resolution in TS projects (tsc --noEmit against a small sample).
maya: I'll coordinate customer comms and link the PR.
ben: follow-up: document publishing playbook: ESM-first is fine but CI must enforce true CJS parity. We'll add that to releases checklist.
alex: ping me on the PR for review.
sam: thanks all — this helps. :thumbsup:
maya: filing the customer incident and adding links once PR landed.
release-bot: note: rollback instructions recorded in the release doc: revert package.json exports to the previous map and republish if hotfix causes regressions.
ben: once hotfix is out, we'll run the updated quickstart across our sample app fleet to catch similar cases.
maya: closing for now, will update thread when PR merges.
